request: MAG-68 — 5. Demote charging.manual_charge_entries.account_id to created_by_account_id. Tier 1 of RM58: the migration, the queries, the four Reader ports, and the cross-module bridge.

tasks.title: Offline check — grep the module's offline test files
tasks.notes: A grep with no schema dependency. May start immediately.

tasks.title: Migration — rename the column, replace two indexes with one
tasks.notes: Design confirmed by the owner at the database gate. No row deleted, no value rewritten, so Down is a true undo.

tasks.title: Queries and sqlc regeneration
tasks.notes: Three reads drop the predicate. UpdateEntry and DeleteEntry KEEP it on the renamed column, per D5. ListEntriesByAccount becomes ListEntriesByVehicles.

tasks.title: Ports and domain type
tasks.notes: Reader drops accountID and keeps int64. Writer.Delete keeps its signature. Entry.AccountID becomes Entry.CreatedByAccountID. No vehicleref import in this tier.

tasks.title: Implementation in service.go
tasks.notes: Must land in the same wave as T6 — go build ./... is red outside internal/charging until it does.

tasks.title: Test fixups inside charging
tasks.notes: The two cross-account tests STAY and keep passing, renamed column only. They are re-keyed onto tesla_id in tier 2. No new test file.

tasks.title: Cross-module bridge — analytics and gateway call sites
tasks.notes: Leader-owned: touches internal/analytics and internal/gateway, outside the charging worker's sandbox. Must land in the same wave as T4.

tasks.title: Docs — AGENTS.md, spec, KB guides
tasks.notes: Touches no Go file. May run in parallel with T4-T6.

tasks.title: Final verification
tasks.notes: Guards plus the repo-wide grep, which must exclude the created_by_ prefix. The suite is the owner's to run.

decisions.what: Database design confirmed: rename the column, drop idx_manual_charge_entries_account_time, replace the vehicle-time index with (tesla_id, charged_on DESC).
decisions.why: No row deleted and no value rewritten, so Down is a true undo. Two indexes become one and it serves all four reads.

decisions.what: UpdateEntry and DeleteEntry keep an account predicate in tier 1, on the renamed column. Tier 2 swaps it for the tesla_id guard. This is the roadmap's D5 and design.md's D4.
decisions.why: Dropping it in tier 1 leaves the write path unauthorized until tier 2. The delete handler proceeds on a lookup miss, so SQL is the only guard, and main auto-deploys.

decisions.what: The artifact worker ran on Opus rather than the default Sonnet.
decisions.why: A DB design gate needs an index plan justified against read patterns plus rejected alternatives. A weak design.md here costs a full re-dispatch and a second user gate.

events.detail: proposal, design, specs/manual-charge-log/spec.md and tasks.md written by the charging worker on Opus. openspec validate --strict passes. Budget for the wave: five_hour_pct 20 -> 47, cost_usd 8.11 -> 20.15.
Owner confirmed the database design. Owner accepted the worker's finding that tier 1 as first written left the write path unauthorized, and chose the transitional predicate instead.

Worker revised design.md D4, the delta spec, tasks.md and proposal.md for the transitional predicate. Corrected its own sqlc expectations: UpdateEntryParams and DeleteEntryParams both survive, renamed field only.

D1 and D5 combined leave reads car-wide and writes author-only for tiers 1-2. On a shared car the co-owner's entries are listed with working-looking controls; update fails with a 500 and delete is a SILENT no-op, because DeleteEntry is :exec and writerService.Delete never checks rows affected. Verified in code by the leader. Tier 3 removes the cause. Not fixed in tier 1 because hiding the controls is gateway work that tier 3 would immediately delete.
